transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Ever since the divorce and moving into my own place, I keep forgetting basic things like paying bills and showing up for appointments, even when I write them down. It’s started causing some real problems for me lately, and I'm just feeling really overwhelmed trying to keep up with it all.

Besides feeling overwhelmed, have you been feeling down or losing interest in things most days, or do these memory problems seem mainly tied to the stress of the divorce and move? When did the forgetfulness start in relation to those events?

I don't feel depressed or lose interest in things, just really overwhelmed and worried about how I'm functioning. While this severe forgetfulness and disorganization became really disruptive about 11 months ago after my divorce, I actually remember having similar struggles with spacing out and losing things back in elementary school.

When you were a child or teenager, did these attention and disorganization problems happen in more than one setting, like both at school and at home, and did they cause trouble with grades, behavior, or daily responsibilities?

Yes, I definitely remember it causing trouble at school when I was young. My elementary school teachers would write on my report cards that I was smart but kept spacing out, losing worksheets, and forgetting to turn in homework I’d actually finished.

Did those attention and organization problems also happen regularly at home or in other parts of your life when you were a child, not just at school? For example, were you often losing things, forgetting chores, or needing lots of reminders?

To be honest, I don't clearly remember how things were at home or if I needed a lot of reminders for chores back then. Most of what I vividly recall is the feedback from my teachers and what was written on my report cards.

As an adult, do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one area of your life, like both at work and at home, or mainly during stressful periods related to the divorce and move? Have they been present pretty consistently even before the divorce?

Yes, they definitely happen in both areas; at home I'm constantly forgetting bills and misplacing my keys, and at work I'll space out during instructions or leave repairs half-finished. While these issues became much more overwhelming and noticeable over the last 11 months after my divorce, they aren't actually new and have been a mild struggle my whole life.

Before the divorce, were these attention and organization problems causing clear problems in your daily life on a regular basis, or were they mostly manageable until the stress of the divorce made them much worse?

Before the divorce, these issues were mostly manageable in my adult life, even though I've always had a tendency to space out. It wasn't until I had to manage my own household, handle my finances alone, and take on a lead role at work that the logistical demands became too much. That's when things really got out of hand and started causing serious problems in my daily life.

When you were a child, before the divorce-related stress of adult life, did your attention and forgetfulness cause clear problems outside school too, like at home, with friends, or in activities? If so, what kinds of problems do you remember?

I'm not really sure, and I don't recall having clear problems outside of school when I was a kid. The issues I do remember from childhood were almost entirely related to school, like what my teachers wrote on my report cards about me spacing out and losing worksheets.
Before age 12, did your attention or forgetfulness cause clear problems in any setting other than school, like at home, with chores, friendships, or activities? If yes, what do you remember?

I don't really remember having clear problems at home, with chores, or with friends back then. I only really recall the school-related issues, like my teachers' comments on my report cards about me spacing out and losing my worksheets.

Do you have anyone or anything that could confirm these attention problems were present before age 12 in daily life, such as a parent, sibling, old report cards, or school records? Or do you think the current problems are mainly a reaction to the divorce and increased responsibilities?

Yes, I actually still have my old elementary school report cards where teachers wrote that I was smart but often spaced out, lost worksheets, and forgot to turn in completed homework. While I initially thought my current struggles were just a reaction to the divorce and my new responsibilities, reflecting on these childhood patterns makes me realize these attention problems have actually been there since I was young.

When life was less stressful before the divorce, did these attention problems still cause noticeable trouble at work, managing your home, or relationships, or were they only a real problem after the divorce? Please give one or two examples.

They only became a major, noticeable struggle after the divorce because of the sudden increase in responsibilities, like managing my household alone and taking on a lead maintenance role at work. Before that, they were mostly manageable, though I actually had similar struggles much earlier in life. For example, in elementary school, my teachers always noted that I was smart but frequently spaced out, lost my worksheets, and forgot to turn in my homework.
Before age 12, do you remember these attention problems causing any clear difficulties outside of school, like at home, in sports, hobbies, or with friends? If yes, what happened?

I don't really recall having any clear difficulties outside of school, like in sports, hobbies, or with friends, before age 12. I mostly just remember the school-related issues, like spacing out in class and losing my worksheets.

Since the divorce and move, have these problems eased as the stress settled, or have they stayed about the same even when things are calmer? Also, before the divorce, did you ever have similar attention problems cause mistakes or missed responsibilities at work or in managing adult life?

The problems have stayed pretty steady over the last 11 months without easing up, even as I've gotten settled. Before the divorce, I didn't face this level of logistical demand with a complex job and managing a household alone, so I didn't really notice these mistakes in my adult life. However, looking further back to my childhood, I definitely had a history of spacing out, losing worksheets, and forgetting homework in elementary school.

Before age 12, did a parent, sibling, or anyone else ever notice that you were also forgetful, disorganized, or needed lots of reminders at home—not just at school? If so, what do you remember them saying or doing?

I don't clearly remember my parents or siblings making specific comments about me being forgetful or disorganized at home back then. However, I vividly recall my elementary school report cards, where teachers always wrote that I was smart but often spaced out, lost worksheets, and forgot to turn in homework I had actually finished.

Between the divorce and move 11 months ago and your lifelong tendency to space out, which feels more true: that stress mainly made an old attention problem much worse, or that these problems only really began because of the divorce? Before the divorce, can you name one adult example of this causing a mistake or missed responsibility, even if it was milder?

It definitely feels like the stress made an old, lifelong problem much worse rather than it being something brand new. However, I can't really recall a specific example of a mistake or missed responsibility as an adult before the divorce, probably because my life was much more structured and shared back then.

If the divorce-related stress were to settle down and your responsibilities became lighter again, do you think these attention problems would mostly go back to being minimal, or would they still clearly interfere with daily life? What makes you think that?

I think they would still be there and interfere with my life because these attention problems aren't actually new, even if the divorce and new responsibilities made them much worse. Looking back, I've had these exact tendencies since childhood, like when my elementary school teachers wrote on my report cards that I was smart but kept spacing out, losing worksheets, and forgetting to turn in my homework.

Before the divorce, when life was more stable, did your attention problems still cause clear difficulties in at least two areas of adult life, like work, home, finances, or relationships? If yes, what were they?

Before the divorce, I don't recall having such clear difficulties in my adult life. My life was much more structured back then, I didn't have to manage everything on my own, and my job was less complex. These issues didn't really surface or cause major problems until all of these recent life changes happened.

Before the divorce, even if things felt manageable overall, did your lifelong spacing out or disorganization ever cause smaller but real problems in adult life—like late bills, missed appointments, losing important items, or mistakes at work? Please give one specific example if you can.

I can't really think of any specific examples of those problems in my adult life before the divorce, as things felt much more manageable and under control back then. However, I do clearly remember having those kinds of issues with spacing out and losing things back in elementary school.

Outside of the divorce and move, have you ever had another period in your adult life when stress was low but you still had the same attention problems causing real impairment? If yes, what was one example?

I can't recall another specific period in my adult life where I had these same severe attention issues during a low-stress time. Before the divorce, my life was much more structured and I had someone else helping to manage things, although I do remember having some of these spacing-out issues way back in childhood.

During the 11 months since the divorce, have your forgetfulness and disorganization been present almost every day, or do they mainly flare up when you’re feeling stressed or thinking about the divorce? When you have a calmer day, do these problems noticeably improve?

These issues have been present pretty steadily almost every day for the last 11 months, rather than just flaring up when I'm stressed or thinking about the divorce. Even on my calmer days, the forgetfulness and disorganization persist and don't really improve.

Do you still have any old report cards or can a parent/sibling confirm that, before age 12, these attention problems also caused trouble outside school—like at home, with chores, or in activities? If yes, what specific problems were noticed?

I don't actually have those physical report cards anymore, and I'm not sure if my family noticed specific issues with chores or activities at home. I just remember the school-related feedback from my teachers about me spacing out, losing worksheets, and forgetting to turn in my homework.

Before age 12, even if you don’t remember details, did anyone ever tell you that you were also forgetful, disorganized, or needed repeated reminders at home or in activities outside school? If yes, who said it and what did they notice?

I don't recall anyone telling me I was forgetful or disorganized at home or in other activities outside of school. However, I vividly remember my elementary school teachers writing on my report cards that I was smart but kept spacing out, losing worksheets, and forgetting to turn in homework I had actually completed.

When you forget bills or appointments now, is it usually because you’re distracted by thoughts or emotions about the divorce, or does it feel like the same kind of spacing out you’ve had since childhood even when you’re not upset? Which of those fits better most of the time?

It definitely feels like the same kind of spacing out I've had since I was a kid, even when I'm feeling completely calm and not thinking about the divorce at all. Managing everything alone now just made the consequences of my forgetfulness much worse, but the actual feeling of losing track of things is the exact same pattern.

Before age 12, can you think of any non-school example of this same spacing out or forgetfulness causing a problem, like losing things during activities, forgetting plans, or needing repeated reminders at home? If so, what happened?

I can't really recall any specific non-school examples of being forgetful or spacing out from when I was a kid. I mostly just remember the feedback from my teachers at school about me losing worksheets and spacing out in class.

Is there a parent, sibling, or anyone who knew you as a child that we could ask whether you had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or in activities before age 12? If yes, what do you think they would say?

I'm not really sure what my family would say since we never really talked about it, but I vividly remember what my elementary school report cards from before age 12 said. My teachers frequently wrote that I was smart but kept spacing out, losing my worksheets, and forgetting to turn in homework I had actually completed.

Since the divorce, have you also had symptoms like constant sadness, anxiety, trouble sleeping, or repeatedly thinking about the divorce, or is the main problem still the same lifelong inattention and disorganization? Which feels like the bigger issue day to day?

While the divorce and move were highly stressful, I don't feel consumed by constant sadness, anxiety, or repetitive thoughts about the relationship itself. The overwhelming daily struggle is definitely the forgetfulness, inattention, and disorganization. Under the pressure of managing my own household and my new job role, this has gotten much worse, but looking back, I realize these attention and organization issues have actually been a pattern since childhood.

Before age 12, besides school, did these same attention problems clearly cause trouble in any other setting, like at home, with chores, sports, hobbies, or friendships? If yes, please give one specific example.

I really only remember these issues affecting my schoolwork and what was written on my report cards. I can't recall any specific examples of them causing significant trouble with my chores, hobbies, or friendships before age 12.

Can you ask a parent, sibling, or someone who knew you well as a child whether you also had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or in activities before age 12? What do you think they would say?

I think my family or anyone who knew me back then would likely agree that I struggled with those things. Looking back, even my elementary school report cards from my teachers constantly mentioned that I was smart but kept spacing out, losing worksheets, and forgetting to turn in homework I had actually finished.

To help tell whether this is lifelong ADHD or mainly stress-related, can you ask a parent, sibling, or someone who knew you before age 12 whether you also had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or during activities outside school? If so, what did they notice?

I haven't actually asked my family or anyone who knew me back then about how I was at home or outside of school, so I'm not really sure what they would say. I only remember what my teachers wrote on my report cards about me spacing out and losing my worksheets.

Would you be willing to check with a parent, sibling, or old records to find out whether, before age 12, you also had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or in activities outside school? If yes, what did they notice?

I'd be happy to check with my family to see what they remember about how I was at home. However, I already recall my old school report cards quite well, where my teachers wrote that I was smart but frequently spaced out, lost worksheets, and forgot to turn in homework I had actually finished.
Before age 12, can you check with a parent or sibling and ask whether you also had the same forgetfulness or disorganization at home or during activities outside school? What do they remember?

I haven't had a chance to talk to my parents or siblings about this yet, so I'm really not sure what they would remember about my behavior at home or outside of school before age 12. I'll have to reach out to them and see if they recall anything.
